Synthetic forward model · SDO/HMI

A 350 m/s velocity that isn't there

Inverting a Zeeman-split, Wilson-deformed umbral line profile with a look-up table calibrated on the quiet Sun turns a profile carrying exactly zero real velocity into a 24-hour oscillation of 150–220 m/s. The period is inherited from OBS_VR, the SDO orbital radial velocity.

Couvidat et al. 2011 algorithmFe I 6173.3433 Å18/18 validation checks passnumpy · scipy · matplotlib only

The hypothesis survives. The mechanism reproduces the right period exactly and lands within a factor of ~1.6–2.4 of the observed residual — but the headline is sharper than the one the specification anticipated: the deformation carries no real velocity signal at all, so the artifact is not an amplified bias, it is a null signal converted into hundreds of m/s by the geometry of the 6-point inversion.

What the pipeline is actually looking at

At 2500 G the longitudinal Zeeman splitting is 111 mÅ — 1.9σ of the line width, equivalent to a 5402 m/s Doppler shift. Each circular polarisation is displaced most of the way to the next filter. The six HMI filters, which sample one 412.8 mÅ "period" of the profile, no longer straddle either line core.

Correction to the specification

§2.2b expected 0.05–0.07 Å at 2500 G. The formula the spec itself supplies, with g = 2.5, gives 0.1112 Å. The code is right and the expected range is too low — it corresponds to g ≈ 1.2, or to B ≈ 1300 G. 0.11 Å at 2500 G is the standard value, and it is why HMI saturates on strong umbral fields.

Experiment A — is the synthetic pipeline honest?

AValidation

z_W = 0, B = 0 · acceptance criterion: |artifact| < 1 m/s

With no deformation the artifact is 8.3 × 10⁻⁸ m/s across v_true ∈ [−3, 3] km/s × OBS_VR ∈ [−3, 3] km/s — seven orders of margin. B_LOS is identically zero.

The uncorrected six-point estimator is not the identity. Its residual reaches 179 m/s over ±7 km/s, and it separates cleanly into two distinct instrumental effects that the specification treated as one:

  • Six-point aliasing — the 5th and 7th harmonics of the profile fold onto the 1st. Peak 83 m/s, and it dominates at ordinary velocities (−12.2 m/s at 2 km/s, against −0.09 m/s of leakage). Periodic in velocity with a 3341 m/s period, which sets the scale for everything that follows.
  • Finite-window leakage — the six filters span exactly one period, so past ±4 km/s the shifted line begins to fall out of the sampled window. Peak 262 m/s, confined to the extremes.

The quiet look-up table inverts all of this to 9 × 10⁻⁸ m/s. Its local gain dv_true/dv_apparent runs from 0.961 to 1.214 — the inversion locally stretches any profile error by up to 21%.

Experiment B — how big, and where does it come from?

BArtifact versus Wilson depression

B = 2500 G · sweep z_W from 0 to 800 km

Structural result — the most important one here

At OBS_VR = 0 the artifact is identically zero (1.8 × 10⁻¹² m/s) for every z_W — not approximately zero. The deformation is symmetric in wavelength, the six filters are symmetric about λ₀, so the LCP and RCP responses are exact mirror images and cancel in V = (v_L + v_R)/2. The quiet table is itself an odd function, so it preserves the cancellation.

The literal Experiment B of the specification — v_true = 0, obs_vr = 0 — therefore returns zero by construction. That is not a bug to fix. The artifact cannot exist without a non-zero total shift: OBS_VR is not merely the modulator, it is the enabling condition. The mechanism predicts the 24-hour signature rather than merely accommodating it.

Evaluated at the orbital maximum, OBS_VR = 3000 m/s:

Experiment C — the temporal signature

C24 hours, inherited exactly

z_W = 600 km · B = 2500 G · v_true = 0 · OBS_VR(t) = 3000·sin(2πt/24h)

The velocity artifact oscillates with a fundamental period of 24.00 h exactly, at 147 m/s amplitude with the specification's look-up table or 223 m/s with an extended one. The waveform is distinctly non-sinusoidal, carrying 29 m/s at 4.8 h and 20 m/s at 8 h — only odd harmonics of the fundamental.

A falsifiable prediction the specification did not anticipate

V is odd in OBS_VR; B_LOS is even in it. So the model predicts a 24-hour oscillation in umbral Dopplergrams accompanied by a 12-hour, ~58 G oscillation in the very same pixels' magnetograms. No real solar velocity field produces that pairing. It is the cheapest and sharpest test this simulation offers.

The largest single uncertainty: extrapolation

With the specification's ±7000 m/s table, 33% of the look-up calls in Experiment C are extrapolations. The table's apparent-velocity range only reaches ±6821 m/s, while an LCP profile at 2500 G with OBS_VR = 3000 m/s presents an apparent velocity near 8.4 km/s.

Rebuilding the table over ±9500 m/s — still inside the ±10023 m/s unambiguous range — removes every extrapolation and raises the predicted amplitude from 147 to 223 m/s. This is exactly Couvidat's caveat that in active regions the correction "becomes a basic extrapolation." The real pipeline uses hmi.lookup_corrected_expanded, an expanded table, so 223 m/s is the more relevant figure. The 147–223 m/s spread is an honest systematic uncertainty of the model, not numerical noise — the look-up grid step is 17 m/s.

Sensitivity — what would it take to reach 350 m/s?

Amplitude versus field strength is not monotone. Below the phase-wrap threshold it is structured, with local maxima near 750, 1500 and 2450 G, because the Zeeman splitting slides the two polarisations along a non-linearity that is periodic in velocity with that 3341 m/s period. Above B ≈ 3250 G the split polarisation plus the orbital shift exceeds the ±10023 m/s unambiguous range, the first-harmonic phase wraps, and the algorithm saturates rather than merely biasing — the steep rise past that point is not a prediction.

Amplitude versus line narrowing grows a little faster than linearly, roughly as the 1.25 power: 5% → 63 m/s, 10% → 147 m/s (the default), 20% → 354 m/s. Twenty percent narrowing at z_W = 600 km is not an unreasonable umbral value, but nothing in this model constrains it independently.

What is robust, and what is calibration

Robust — instrument geometry, no free parameters

  • The six-point Fourier estimator is non-linear, with a residual periodic in velocity at 3341 m/s and a finite-window breakdown past ±4 km/s.
  • The quiet table corrects that non-linearity only for a quiet-width profile; its local gain reaches 1.21.
  • A wavelength-symmetric umbral deformation yields exactly zero artifact at zero total shift — the artifact is switched on by OBS_VR and inherits its period exactly.
  • V is odd and B_LOS is even in OBS_VR → 24 h in velocity, 12 h in the magnetogram.
  • Only line width matters. Ic and Id cancel identically in the first Fourier harmonic — verified to 2.7 × 10⁻¹² m/s. K_C and K_D have no effect whatsoever; the entire Wilson calibration collapses to K_S.

Calibration-dependent — refine before quoting a number

  • K_S, the line narrowing per km of Wilson depression: 10% at 600 km here, 20% needed for 350 m/s.
  • The Gaussian shape itself. A real umbral Fe I 6173 in LCP is not a shifted Gaussian — it retains a π component and unsplit stray light, giving a double-humped profile with far more power at the 5th harmonic, which is precisely the harmonic that aliases. This model therefore likely under-predicts.
  • A_orb = 3000 m/s and the assumed sinusoidal OBS_VR.

Where this leaves the claim

A profile deformation carrying zero real velocity is turned by the HMI six-point inversion into a 24-hour oscillation of 150–220 m/s under realistic umbral parameters, alongside a 12-hour, ~58 G oscillation in the magnetogram. Right period, right structure, within a factor of 1.6–2.4 of the observed 350 m/s — and reachable inside the plausible range of the one calibration parameter that matters.

What this does not establish is that 350 m/s specifically is the predicted number. The amplitude depends on K_S, on the true umbral profile shape, and on the real table's velocity coverage. Two things would settle it: a Milne-Eddington synthesis of the umbral Stokes profiles in place of the shifted Gaussian, and validation against the actual hmi.lookup_corrected_expanded table.
